one_large_narrow_integer.row_formula: id=1..N; bucket=MOD(id,1024); measure/payload are seeded modular integers

sparse_skewed_unsigned_primary_keys.row_formula: id=seq*100000 as BIGINT UNSIGNED; 90% of rows have bucket 0

several_large_tables.row_formula: each table has N deterministic rows; table index changes the seeded measures

many_small_relational_tables.row_formula: N total rows split evenly across eight tables; each table links to its predecessor by nullable parent_id

wide_utf8_text_json_decimal.row_formula: fixed-seed Unicode label and repeated text, JSON numeric value=id, DECIMAL(30,12) value=id/1000

binary_large_rows.row_formula: fixed-seed 81920-byte LONGBLOB pattern includes NUL/high-bit bytes; optional VARBINARY cycles through NULL, empty and 16-byte values

bad_rows_fixed_rate.row_formula: id=1..N; payload contains CHAR(0) at each predeclared 0.1%, 1%, or 5% ID interval

notes: The narrow and sparse workloads use one table; the large-table workload uses four tables; the relational workload uses eight linked tables.
All generated values are deterministic; the sparse-key workload uses unsigned BIGINT keys and the relational case checks seven foreign keys.
Integer-shaped profiles use 28 canonical payload bytes per row before row/index/page overhead; wide-row logical payload bytes are measured from source and target values.
The memory profiles exceed the loader memory limit; do not run them without an isolated capacity plan.
